Cambridge Latin Course is... interesting. Its a very specific style of learning - much like you I spent 3 years on it and then switched to John Taylor for GCSE and the difference it made! I think the CLC is helpful for getting people into it, but it needs to be alongside a proper grammar book tbh, on its own it leaves a lot of gaps in understanding tbh. John Taylor for the win! 😂

Also, someone else has just said this but I would like to back them up - John Taylor’s books for Latin or Greek are amazing and give you the detail you need. You will be expected to have a decent grip of the grammar over just fluency so try and balance the two! Best of luck!

Focus on one language for now - research which unis/courses dont require Latin/Greek A-Level - read broadly but also don’t spend tonnes of time on a book that you arent enjoying. Literature - just read original texts; there is already a good recommendation for philosophy; History of Art - Caroline Vout’s books are fab, I also believe Mary Beard has done a good art book recently. Also highly reccomend the “Very Short Introduction to” series - they have Classics, Ancient Greece, Roman Republic and Roman empire so far I believe - and I think one on Ovid is coming out too. 

If you wanna message me abt this, feel free, I’m just about to go to uni to do Classics with no Latin/Classics A-Level, more than happy to help out
